newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ member says watching economy closely--media.
newsitem.headline: BOJ member says watching economy closely--media.

text.p: A newly appointed member of the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) policy board has said he will keep close watch over the Japanese economy to see whether the gradual recovery will continue without pause, media reports said on Tuesday.

"The issue is whether the trend of gradual economic recovery will continue without interruption. At the moment, I can only say that we will be watching economic movements deeply and widely," Susumu Taketomi was quoted as saying by the Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun in an interview with a selected group of journalists on Monday.

He was quoted by the newspaper as saying that easy monetary policy was aimed at preventing any negative impact from excessive falls in prices in order to prevent any unnecessary uncertainty about the economy among firms and households.
Prices have generally stopped falling and business and consumer sentiment has improved, he said.

Taketomi was quoted as saying that although he understood the difficulties faced by people who depend on interest income, monetary policy decisions should not be made for the sake of a particular industrial sector or certain economic entities, but should be for the purpose of macro-economic management.

"The Japanese economy is on a gradual recovery trend. I would like to determine the effect of the consumption tax hike on housing investments and durable goods. Although the economy may slow down, the overall economic recovery trend will not be damaged. We need to see whether the recovery will be secure," Taketomi was quoted as saying in the interview.
Kyodo news agency said in a report on the interview that Taketomi expressed a cautious view about changing the course of the country's monetary policy.
